claim: Bradley, Jordan and Ritter (J. Finance 2003): 1,611 US IPOs 1996-2000; quiet period ends after the 25th calendar day (day 0 = 26th calendar day or first trading day thereafter); analyst coverage initiated immediately for 76%; initiated firms earn a five-day (-2,+2) abnormal return of 4.1% vs 0.1% for firms with no coverage (Nasdaq-adjusted); abnormal returns concentrate in the days just before expiry. Excludes offers with file-range midpoint below $8.
quote: return of 4.1 percent versus 0.1 percent for firms with no coverage.
limitations: 1996-2000 bubble sample, Nasdaq-adjusted, no transaction costs, the quiet period then ran 25 calendar days; no post-2000 replication found in this pass.
impact_on_spec: Defines the A-family calendar (QP day, market-adjusted CAR) and the numbers the plan's stop conditions are set against.

claim: FINRA Regulatory Notice 15-30 (August 2015): Rule 2241 reduces the 40-day and 25-day IPO quiet periods to a minimum of 10 days after the offering for members that acted as underwriter or dealer (effective 2015-12-24). The mandatory research blackout that made day 25 a hard date in 1996-2000 no longer exists in the 2016-2026 sample; any day-25 clustering of initiations would be a convention, not a rule.
quote: The rule therefore reduces the current 40-day and 25-day IPO quiet periods to a minimum
limitations: Regulatory text; says nothing about when underwriters actually initiate coverage in 2016-2026 (no local analyst-initiation data), so the QP-day calendar could still be a habit.
impact_on_spec: Directly weakens the mechanism for the whole local sample; motivates a non-gating diagnostic window at day 10 and a hard stop if the day-25 window shows nothing.

claim: Ritter and Welch (J. Finance 2002): underwriters are prohibited from initiating analyst coverage for 25 calendar days after an IPO; managing underwriters typically initiate at the end of the quiet period, usually with a buy or strong buy.

claim: Ritter (Annual Review of Financial Economics 2011): the average equally weighted return in the three years after an IPO is low, not counting the first-day return; first-day returns are large when the offer price is revised upward during registration.
quote: equally weighted return in the three years after an IPO is low, not counting the first-day return.
limitations: Three-year buy-and-hold on all IPOs; says nothing about the week 2-8 calendar windows tested here.
impact_on_spec: Background for the B-family (post-first-week decay) direction.

claim: Wolf Richter (Wolf Street, 2025-12-29): 202 IPOs in 2025 excluding 144 SPACs, much of the volume foreign micro-IPOs; of the 20 largest, 14 traded below the IPO price on 2025-12-26 and 11 had plunged more than 40% from their intraday high after first-day pops.
quote: Of the largest 20 IPOs, 14 trade below their IPO price; only 6 trade above it. Many plunged from their post-IPO pop.
limitations: Blog, largest-20 sample chosen after the fact, prices from the IPO price (not available locally), no costs or borrow.
impact_on_spec: Motivation for the B family; the local proxy R5 is measured from the first open, not the offer price.
